archetype.name: Lost Season
archetype.definition: A year with nothing to play for by the turn of the calendar: Sacramento ranked in the league's bottom five on both ends, never had a winning month, and finished last in the Pacific by a wide distance.

report.headline: Sacramento's slide from 48 wins bottoms out in a 22-60 lost season

recap.finish: 22-60, fifth in the Pacific; missed the postseason
recap.body:
This was a team without a calling card on either end. The Kings finished with a -10.1 Net Rtg, 28th in the league, built from the 26th-ranked offense (111.4 ORtg) and the 28th-ranked defense (121.5 DRtg). Three seasons ago this franchise had the league's best offense and went 48-34. The record has fallen every year since, and this was the year the floor gave way.

There was no real arc to speak of, only a steady grind. The Kings opened 1-4 in October and went 4-12 in November. They were 12-38 by the end of January and 14-47 after a 2-9 February. Somewhere in there sat a 16-game losing streak, and the longest winning run all year was four. The 3-3 April was the only month they didn't lose, and it came against a closing ten-game stretch (3-7, -10.3 a game) that matched the season almost exactly. Nothing late in the year pointed to a turn.

The offense's problem was the shape of it. Sacramento took the smallest share of its shots from three in the league, a 33.9 3PA Rate that ranked 30th and sat 7.6 points under the league average. It also made only 34% of them, 29th. A team that put up a 43.2 rate two seasons ago became a mid-range team without the shot-making to justify it, and its eFG % of 52.5 ranked 29th. Turnovers (12.6 TOV %, 13th) and offensive rebounding (13th) were fine, but neither moves the needle when the shots themselves are this inefficient.

The defense was worse, and it was a familiar story. Opponents shot a 57.2 eFG % (29th) and 37.9% from three. Shooting guards did the most damage: they scored 30.89 points a game against Sacramento, 27th in the league and about two points over their own averages. Defense has ranked in the bottom third in four of the last five seasons here, so this isn't new. This year the offense simply stopped covering for it.

If anything the 22 wins flattered them. The margin implied 19, and the +3 W vs Pt Diff ranked fourth-luckiest in the league. The roster grades read like the record: backcourt D, wings D-, frontcourt F.

highlights.title: DeRozan's efficient volume held up
highlights.body: DeMar DeRozan played 77 games and scored 1,419 points on 59.4 TS %, and his 5.6 Win Shares were the most on the team by a distance. In a league that rewards threes, he stayed productive in a mid-range-heavy offense. Still, the team was worse with him on the floor (-4.9 On-Off), so his scoring didn't turn into winning minutes.

highlights.title: Bigs finished efficiently
highlights.body: Maxime Raynaud scored 922 points on 61.9 TS % and grabbed 556 rebounds over 74 games. Behind him, Dylan Cardwell (+7.5) and Precious Achiuwa (+5.4) had two of the best On-Off marks on the roster. The listed frontcourt produced 14.6 Win Shares, far more than the guards and wings combined. It is the one group with pieces that play like NBA rotation players on a bad team.

lowlights.title: A defense with no stopping point
lowlights.body: The 121.5 DRtg ranked 28th and sat 5.8 points worse than the league. Opponents shot a 57.2 eFG % and 37.9% from three, and shooting guards scored 30.89 points a game against this team. The defense had already been bottom-third in four of the last five years, so this is structural, not a one-year dip.

lowlights.title: The three-point shot disappeared
lowlights.body: Sacramento's 33.9 3PA Rate was last in the league, and its 34% from deep was 29th. Two years ago the rate was 43.2. Taking fewer threes and making them poorly left an offense that ranked 26th, down from seventh a season earlier.

lowlights.title: Perimeter minutes went nowhere
lowlights.body: The wings graded D- and the backcourt D, and their listed players produced only 1.7 and 2.5 Win Shares. Russell Westbrook carried a 25.9 USG % on 52.8 TS %, and De'Andre Hunter's -7.2 On-Off was the worst on the roster. Zach LaVine's 61.4 TS % was a bright spot, but he played just 39 games.

arc.note: Losing records in every month from October through March, a 16-game losing streak along the way, and a 3-3 April that changed nothing. The final ten games played out at the season's exact level.

recap.nextYear: The usable production sits up front. DeRozan was the team's most productive player, and Raynaud, Achiuwa and Cardwell gave efficient, positive minutes, even if the frontcourt's F grade says they don't rank well league-wide. The guards and wings need the most work: neither group graded above D, and they defended poorly at the point of attack. The three-point rate has to come back toward where it was two years ago for the offense to have a ceiling. One caution: 22 wins already ran three ahead of what the margin implied, so the real starting point is closer to a 19-win team, and the late-season numbers show no hidden improvement.

confidence.note: Full 82-game sample, both ends consistently bottom-five.
